draft.title: Forming and justifying an opinion
card: An opinion is what you think about a character, setting or event in a text. A good response states the opinion clearly, for example: "Zara is brave."
To justify an opinion, give a reason. The reason explains why you think it, for example: "She faces danger to protect her little brother."
Then add a detail from the text that supports the reason. This can be something a character does or says, or something the narrator describes. Use your own words or a short quote.
Other readers may form a different opinion about the same text. Your opinion is still sound if your reasons and details come from the text.
draft.remember: Say what you think, give a reason, then back it up with a detail from the text.

a.q: Which sentence best justifies the opinion that Jai is a loyal friend?
opts: He stays by Sam's hospital bed all night, though he is tired
Jai is a character in the story who has a friend named Sam
Most readers agree that Jai is a really good friend to Sam
I like Jai because I have a friend who is a lot like him
a.why: The right answer gives a detail from the text that shows loyalty. The last option is a personal link, so it does not use the text. The other two only name the character or say what others think.
a.clue: Which option points to something that happens in the story?

b.q: Ella thinks the town in a novel feels lonely. Her classmate Ben thinks it feels peaceful. What should Ella do to make her opinion sound?
opts: Give reasons and details from the text that show loneliness
Say that Ben is wrong because the teacher agrees with her
Change her opinion to match Ben's so that they agree
Say the town is lonely because she would feel lonely there
b.why: An opinion is sound when reasons and details from the text support it. Ben's different view does not make hers wrong. Her own feelings about the town are not evidence from the text.
b.clue: A sound opinion can differ from another reader's. What must it rest on?

a.best: He stays by Sam's hospital bed all night, though he is tired

b.best: Give reasons and details from the text that show loneliness

problems.detail: Why (a) calls 'the last option' the personal link, but in the order shown the personal-link option ('I like Jai because I have a friend…') is first. The last option is 'Most readers agree…'. Because the options are shuffled, the explanation points students to the wrong option. It should name the option by its content, not its position.
The clue asks 'What must it rest on?', but the card only says an opinion 'is still sound if' its reasons and details come from the text. 'Must' is stronger than the card's wording.
